name: a-crayon-dismissing-hand
prompt: Vertical illustration made with a black grease crayon dragged across rough, ridged drawing board, with thin grey ink washes laid underneath, so every dark breaks into a grainy stipple of tiny dots and the blacks look soft, smeared and thumb-blended at the edges, like a hand-drawn magazine plate from about 1919. Very close and from low down: in the lower third, sharply drawn and huge in the frame, a plump gloved hand with a thick wrist and a cufflinked starched cuff flicks outward, fingers splayed mid-shoo, the dismissive gesture caught at its peak. Just above and behind it, still crisp, the heavy jowled profile of a well-fed gentleman in a tall silk top hat, double chin pressed into a high wing collar, a waxed moustache, eyelids half-lowered in boredom, the dark curve of an iron park-bench arm under his elbow. Further back, smudged and out of focus as if rubbed with a finger, a gaunt young soldier in a rumpled army greatcoat leans on a wooden crutch, one trouser leg pinned empty below the knee, his tired eyes fixed on the hand. Dusk: a single gas lamp outside the frame to the right throws long raking crayon shadows diagonally across the board and leaves a rim of pale paper along the gentleman's hat brim and knuckles. The upper third is nearly empty, a deep velvety grey-black dusk wash with only a few bare branches faintly scratched in, left clear for a caption. Palette strictly black, charcoal grey and warm off-white paper tone, no colour. No lettering, captions, speech balloons or marks of any kind drawn in. Thanks.
